S01.title: Read the product and what it sells
S01.purpose: Build one dated fact sheet of what the product does, what it costs, and what is still unknown, so every later sentence of sales copy can be checked against something real.

steps.do: Open the product's own pages: home page, sales page, pricing page, and any help or delivery documents. Write down each URL and the date and time you read it.
steps.evidence: A list of URLs or file names, each with the time it was read.

steps.do: Look at the live product or a demo and list what a user can actually get done with it today. Ask the owner about anything you cannot see for yourself.
steps.evidence: Each listed function points to a screen, a document page, or the owner's confirmation.

steps.do: For each item on that list, mark whether the software does it, a person does it as a service, or it is not delivered yet.
steps.evidence: Every item is labeled software, human service, or not yet available, with who delivers it and any limit.

steps.do: Write down what is for sale: plan names, price, currency, billing period, current discounts, and when each discount ends. If a price is not shown on the product's pages, write 'unknown' and ask the owner.
steps.evidence: Every price and term has the URL or owner message it came from.

steps.do: Open the existing trial, sign-up, and buy links and check that each one loads and lands on the right product. Do not fill in forms and do not pay.
steps.evidence: Each link is listed with the page it actually reached and whether it worked.

steps.do: Collect proof that may be quoted: real customer cases, screenshots, numbers, and statements the owner has approved for public use.
steps.evidence: Each piece of proof has a source and a note on where it may be used.

steps.do: List what must never be promised without the owner's say: features that do not exist, new prices, extra deliverables, and business limits.
steps.evidence: A 'do not promise' list that later posts and replies can be checked against.

steps.do: Put everything into one product fact sheet: what is sold, proof, links, limits, and unknowns. Date it so later steps know which version they used.
steps.evidence: One dated fact sheet that the following steps can use without reopening the site.

steps.do: Note when the sources should be checked again, and update the fact sheet whenever the owner says something changed.
steps.evidence: A next-check date written on the fact sheet.

blockers.do: If the product pages will not load, ask the owner for a working URL or the page text, and do not describe the product from memory.
If no price is visible, record the price as unknown and ask the owner; never guess one.
If the product can only be seen after signing in, ask the owner for screenshots or a short walk-through; never ask for a password.
If two pages state different prices or features, list both versions with their URLs and ask the owner which one is current.
If a sign-up or buy link fails or lands on the wrong page, report it to the owner before any post sends people there.

deliver_help.product_facts: What the product does today, one fact per line, each with its source URL. Example: 'Turns a YouTube link into a piano score PDF (source: home page)'.
deliver_help.offer_and_price: Plans, price, currency, billing period, discounts, and the buy link, each with its source. Write 'unknown' where the page does not say.
deliver_help.limits_and_unknowns: What the product does not do, what must not be promised, and every question still open for the owner.

A-VOC.title: Collect real buyer quotes
A-VOC.purpose: Gather the exact words real people use for this problem and the result they want, because copy written in buyers' own words gets read and copy written in the seller's words gets skipped.

steps.do: List where real buyers talk about this problem: interviews, reviews, public help threads, customer emails, and refund reasons. Mark which of these the owner allows you to use.
steps.evidence: A source list with the URL or origin of each source and whether its use is allowed.

steps.do: Collect at least five posts or comments where real people describe this problem in their own words. For each one keep the shortest exact quote, its URL, its date, and an anonymous label such as 'person 1' instead of a name.
steps.evidence: At least five quotes, each with URL, date, and anonymous label.

steps.do: Sort each quote under one of five headings: the situation they were in, what they do today, what it costs them, the result they want, and what makes them hesitate before buying.
steps.evidence: Every quote sits under one heading.

steps.do: Remove sellers promoting themselves, AI-written answers, and guesses with no source. If you cannot read the original text, mark it as missing and do not paraphrase it from memory.
steps.evidence: A list of what was removed and why.

steps.do: Note which kind of people the sample came from (people who have not bought, buyers, people who refunded) and state its limits. Do not present it as the whole market.
steps.evidence: A short note on who is in the sample and who is missing.

blockers.do: If you find fewer than five real quotes, ask the owner for customer emails or reviews, say which public places you searched, and label everything else as a guess.
If a page is blocked or needs sign-in, skip it or ask the owner for a copy; do not rebuild the quote from search snippets.
If the only material is private customer messages, ask the owner whether they may be used and remove names before using them.
If a quote exposes health, money, or relationship details about an identifiable person, drop the identifying details and keep only the need that relates to the product.

deliver_help.buyer_quotes: Exact quotes with an anonymous label and date. Example: 'person 3, 2026-10-02: I spent a whole weekend writing this out by hand'.
deliver_help.sources: The URL or origin of every quote, and the time you read it.
deliver_help.patterns_found: What repeats across quotes, grouped as situation, current workaround, cost, wanted result, and hesitation.
deliver_help.limits_and_unknowns: Who the sample leaves out, what you could not read, and anything that is still a guess.

A-SEGMENTS.title: Group buyers by situation and trigger
A-SEGMENTS.purpose: Split buyers into groups by the moment the problem shows up, then choose one group to speak to, because a post aimed at one clear situation gets more clicks than a post aimed at everyone.

steps.do: Read the collected quotes and the product fact sheet. Do not work out why people buy from their age or gender.
steps.evidence: Each observation points to a quote or a product fact.

steps.do: Group buyers by five things: when the problem shows up, what they use instead today, what that costs them, the result they want, and the time, money, or skill they have.
steps.evidence: Two to four named groups, each described on those five points.

steps.do: Attach at least one real quote to each group, or label the group as a guess. For each group, say who is not a fit.
steps.evidence: Each group shows its quote or the word 'guess', plus who it leaves out.

steps.do: Leave ability to pay, who decides, budget, and timing as 'unknown' unless a source says otherwise. Do not answer these from a job title.
steps.evidence: A list of unknowns for each group.

steps.do: Choose the one group you can reach on Threads now and that the product can serve today. Record why you chose it and what would show the choice is wrong.
steps.evidence: The chosen group, the reason, and at least one case that argues against it.

blockers.do: If there are no buyer quotes, go back and collect them; if the owner wants to continue anyway, label every group as a guess.
If all you have is age, gender, or job title, do not build groups from it; ask the owner about three recent buyers and what happened just before they bought.
If the best-supported group needs something the product does not do, choose the next group and report the gap to the owner.
If two groups differ only in name, keep the one with more quotes and drop the other.

deliver_help.buyer_groups: Two to four groups, each with its trigger moment and a supporting quote or the word 'guess'. Example: 'Parents whose child has a recital in two weeks'.
deliver_help.chosen_group: The one group this round of posts will speak to.
deliver_help.why_chosen: Why this group is reachable and can be served now, and what result would prove the choice wrong.
deliver_help.unknowns: Budget, who decides, and timing questions that no source has answered yet.

A-MOTIVES.title: Map each problem to a buying motive
A-MOTIVES.purpose: Connect each stated problem to the deeper result the buyer wants, because people pay for a change in their life or work, not for a feature.

steps.do: For each group, reread the real quotes and separate the problem they have right now from the change they want in their life or work.
steps.evidence: Each group has a 'problem now' line and a 'change wanted' line, both tied to quotes.

steps.do: Give each motive a working label such as earning money or career, love or company, health, looks, being liked, saving time, independence, or belonging. Treat every label as a guess to be tested.
steps.evidence: A list of motives, each with its label and marked 'to be tested'.

steps.do: For each motive write the quote behind it, the situation, how confident you are, and any quote that points the other way. Do not infer sensitive weaknesses from personal data.
steps.evidence: Each motive has a quote, a confidence note (strong, some, or guess), and any opposing quote.

steps.do: Split each motive into three parts: the practical job they want done, how they want to feel, and how they want others to see them.
steps.evidence: Each motive lists its practical, emotional, and social part, with 'unknown' where there is no evidence.

steps.do: Keep only the parts the product can really help with. Do not inflate fear, and do not promise income, health, or relationship outcomes.
steps.evidence: A final list of motives the product can serve, plus the ones you dropped and why.

blockers.do: If a motive has no quote behind it, mark it as a guess and go back to collect buyer quotes before relying on it.
If a motive does not fit the common labels, describe it in the buyer's own words and do not force it into one.
If the product does not really help with a motive, drop it from the selling plan and tell the owner what buyers wanted.
If a motive depends on guessing someone's health, finances, or relationship status, remove it and use only needs people stated themselves.

deliver_help.motives: Each motive in one line, with its group. Example: 'Wants to play the song at the recital without paying a teacher to transcribe it'.
deliver_help.supporting_quotes: The quote and source behind each motive, plus any quote that contradicts it.
deliver_help.guesses_to_test: Motives with no quote behind them yet, clearly marked as guesses.
deliver_help.limits: Outcomes the product cannot deliver and so must not be promised.

A-PRIORITY.title: Pick the strongest motive and objection
A-PRIORITY.purpose: Choose the single motive and the single objection that matter most to the chosen group right now, so the post makes one strong point and not five weak ones.

steps.do: For the chosen group, read the list of motives, what they use today, and the event that makes them look for a solution. Count repeated quotes from the same person once.
steps.evidence: The group name and the quotes used, with repeats from one person merged.

steps.do: Compare the motives on four points: how strong the quotes are, how urgent the timing is, what the buyer already pays or loses, and how much of it the product can help with. Judge by this evidence, not by scoring a fixed list of desires.
steps.evidence: A short comparison showing each motive against the four points.

steps.do: Name the main motive, the second motive, and the cases that contradict them. If the evidence is thin, keep two candidates and say so.
steps.evidence: Main and second motive, opposing cases, and a plain statement of how sure you are.

steps.do: Separate people who have the budget and the authority to buy from people who only want it. List unknown buying obstacles as questions to ask.
steps.evidence: Known objections, plus a list of open questions for the owner or for buyers.

steps.do: Pass the main motive on to the benefits step and the angle test. Write down beforehand which real replies or payments would prove it wrong.
steps.evidence: The main motive in one sentence and what result would disprove it.

blockers.do: If the ranking rests on no buyer quotes, say it is a guess and go back to collect quotes before treating it as settled.
If the quotes cannot separate two motives, keep both and let the angle test compare them.
If nothing shows who has the budget or the say, leave it unknown and ask the owner who has actually paid before.
If the owner believes a different motive is strongest, record both views with their evidence and test both.

deliver_help.main_motive: One sentence, with the quote that best supports it.
deliver_help.main_objection: The strongest reason this group hesitates to buy, or 'unknown' if no source says. Example: 'Not sure the score will be accurate enough to play from'.
deliver_help.second_motive: The runner-up, or a second candidate if the evidence could not separate them.
deliver_help.what_would_disprove_it: The reply, click, or payment result that would show the main motive is wrong.
deliver_help.open_questions: Budget, authority, and timing questions still unanswered.

A-LADDER.title: Turn features into benefits you can prove
A-LADDER.purpose: Translate each real feature into the benefit and result a buyer cares about, and mark exactly where proof stops, so the post is persuasive and still true.

steps.do: Read the product facts, the limits, and the buyer quotes one at a time. Do not add anything the product cannot do.
steps.evidence: The facts and quotes you used, each traceable to the fact sheet or a source URL.

steps.do: For each feature write a chain of four items: the feature, the benefit a buyer can observe, the result they want, and the point past which nothing may be promised.
steps.evidence: One chain per feature with all four items filled in.

steps.do: Mark each link in every chain as verified, guess, or unsupported, and give the reason.
steps.evidence: Every link carries one of the three marks and its basis.

steps.do: Check every number and every cause-and-effect claim separately. For example, 'meet people from five industries' and 'raise your chance of a new job' are two claims, and each needs its own proof.
steps.evidence: A list of claims, each with its proof or the note 'no proof, do not state as fact'.

steps.do: Choose the value statement that is both true and matches the main motive, and write it as one to three short message options ready to test.
steps.evidence: The chosen statement and its message options, each tied to verified facts.

blockers.do: If the product fact sheet is missing or out of date, go back and read the product before writing any benefit.
If a benefit has no proof, word it as an invitation to try or as something being tested, never as a result.
If a number has no source, remove it or ask the owner where it comes from.
If the benefit buyers want depends on a feature that does not exist, drop it from the copy and tell the owner about the gap.

deliver_help.chosen_message: The one true statement that best matches the main motive. Example: 'Paste a YouTube link and get a playable piano score in minutes'.
deliver_help.message_options: One to three short ways of saying it, for testing.
deliver_help.facts_used: The product facts and sources each option relies on.
deliver_help.must_not_promise: Results and numbers that have no proof and must stay out of the copy.

A-ANGLES.title: Design the sales angle test
A-ANGLES.purpose: Set up a fair comparison of two or three ways to present the same true benefit, with the win rule written before posting, so the numbers decide which one earns more link clicks.

steps.do: Name one buyer group in one situation, the quote that represents them, the motive, and the benefit the product can deliver.
steps.evidence: Group, quote, motive, and benefit written in four short lines.

steps.do: Write two or three angles: the progress they hope for, getting past the real obstacle, and a believable demonstration. Do not use fear to exaggerate outcomes.
steps.evidence: Two or three angles, each in one or two sentences.

steps.do: For each angle list the facts that support it, the promises that are still unknown, and the wording that must not be used.
steps.evidence: Each angle has supporting facts, unknowns, and banned wording next to it.

steps.do: Change only one thing between versions and keep the same channel, audience, and destination link. Before posting, write the guess being tested, how long the test runs, the number that counts as a win, and the cost in time or money.
steps.evidence: A test plan written before the first post, showing the guess, the duration, the win number, and the cost.

steps.do: Choose the main number: qualified inquiries, sign-ups, payments, or another number named in advance (in this playbook, link clicks divided by views). Likes are supporting information only, and state when the test stops.
steps.evidence: The main number, the rule for stopping, and the versions ready to be written as posts.

blockers.do: If no main motive has been chosen, go back and choose one before writing angles.
If an angle only works with a claim that has no proof, rewrite it as an invitation to try or drop the angle.
If the account is too small for the versions to get comparable views, say so and report the result as an early signal, not as proof.
If link clicks cannot be read anywhere, ask the owner how they can be checked, and do not declare a winner from likes.

deliver_help.test_guess: One sentence. Example: 'Leading with the recital deadline gets a higher link click rate than leading with the price'.
deliver_help.angles: The two or three angles, with the one thing that differs between them.
deliver_help.facts_used: The product facts and buyer quotes each angle relies on.
deliver_help.win_rule: The main number, how long the test runs, and the result that counts as a win. Example: 'Link clicks divided by views after 48 hours; the higher version wins if each has at least 300 views'.

S10.purpose: 安排下一批內容與素材

steps.do: 讀取目標與上輪結論：確認這批內容要解決哪個問題或測什麼差異。
steps.evidence: 每個項目能對應流程目標。

steps.do: 盤點可重用素材：檢查舊文、圖片、影片、示範與權利。
指定買家與階段：每項內容只設定清楚的主要對象。
選切角與證據：列問題、承諾、真實示範及可用案例。

A-COPY.title: Write the post from proven facts
A-COPY.purpose: Write the Threads post that opens with the buyer's own situation and offers one true step forward with a link, because a specific, believable post is what makes a reader click through to the product site.

steps.do: Check every sentence against the fact sheet and against the way the owner writes. Remove any number without support, or reword it as a clearly labeled guess.

blockers.do: If no angle has been chosen, go back to the angle test step before writing.

C-THREADS-ACCESS.title: Confirm the Threads account and who publishes
C-THREADS-ACCESS.purpose: Settle which Threads account will post and who presses publish (the owner, or the agent's own browser), so the post goes out under the right brand without the owner being stopped halfway.

steps.do: Ask the owner for the URL of the Threads profile that will post. Note separately which Threads account and which Instagram account are signed in right now; being signed in to Instagram does not mean the Threads profile exists.
steps.evidence: Both handles written down, with whether each profile exists.

steps.do: Open the Threads profile URL as a public page and confirm that it exists and belongs to the owner. If it exists, use it and do not create a second profile.
steps.evidence: The profile URL and the owner's confirmation that it is theirs.

steps.do: Decide who presses publish: the owner on their own device, or the agent's own browser if it is already signed in to that account. If nobody is signed in, the owner signs in themselves on the official Threads screen and, if it offers 'Continue with Instagram', checks the Instagram handle shown first. Never ask for a password.
steps.evidence: Who will publish, how the owner signed in, and the handle that was selected.

steps.do: Create a new Threads profile only if the owner asked for one in this conversation. Check the name, bio, and website link with the owner, and never enter a made-up birthday or made-up verification details.
steps.evidence: The owner's request and the profile details they approved, or a note that no new profile was needed.

steps.do: If Threads asks for a verification code, acceptance of terms, or an identity check, stop and tell the owner exactly which screen needs them. Note where you stopped and return to the same profile once they have finished.
steps.evidence: A note of what the owner needs to do, on which screen, and where to resume.

steps.do: After sign-in or profile creation, open the public profile again and the account's own profile screen. Confirm the handle matches the brand and that whoever publishes can open the new post box.
steps.evidence: Profile URL, handle, confirmation that a new post can be started, and the time this was checked.

blockers.do: If the Instagram account offered at sign-in is not the one tied to the intended Threads profile, have the owner go back to the account chooser and pick the right handle.
If the Threads URL shows no profile, tell the owner; a successful Instagram sign-in is not a Threads profile, and a new one is created only if the owner asks.
If a verification code, terms screen, or identity check appears, stop and tell the owner which screen and which button; never enter codes or accept terms for them.
If the agent's browser is not signed in to the right account, set who_publishes to 'owner' and plan to hand them the final text to post.
If the signed-in account is a personal account or a different brand, stop before any posting and ask the owner which account to use.

deliver_help.account_handle: The Threads handle that will post. Example: '@notavue'.
deliver_help.profile_url: The public URL of that profile, opened and confirmed to exist.
deliver_help.who_publishes: 'owner' or 'agent browser', plus one line on why.

C-TH-METRICS.title: Read views and link clicks on Threads
C-TH-METRICS.purpose: Record views and link clicks for the account's posts, before and after the new post, so the link click rate (link clicks divided by views) can be compared using real numbers.

steps.do: Confirm which Threads profile and which posts you are measuring, the date range, and the time zone. Check whether you can open the Threads insights screen; if you cannot, ask the owner for a screenshot or the numbers.
steps.evidence: Profile handle, post URLs, date range with time zone, and how the numbers will be obtained.

steps.do: Read the follower count at the start and end of the range, plus views, replies, and link clicks where Threads shows them. Write 'not shown' for any number Threads does not display, and do not estimate it.
steps.evidence: The numbers exactly as displayed, with the screen they came from and the time they were read.

steps.do: Count conversations once per person who shows a real need for the product. Do not count the owner's or the agent's own replies as new prospects.
steps.evidence: The number of different people who asked about the product, with the URL of each reply.

steps.do: Add website visits and sales only if the owner already has a source for them, such as site analytics or payment records. Where you cannot tell which post led to a visit or a sale, say so plainly.
steps.evidence: Each visit or sales figure names its source, and unknown links between post and sale are stated.

blockers.do: If you cannot open the Threads insights screen, ask the owner for a screenshot of it or for the two numbers: views and link clicks.
If Threads shows no link clicks for the post, ask the owner for clicks from the site analytics or link tool they already use and name that source; otherwise record 'not available'.
If the account has no earlier posts with a link, record the baseline as 'none' and state that the first post sets it.
If the screenshot or screen shows a different handle from the agreed one, do not use those numbers and ask again.
If the post is less than 24 hours old, report the numbers as early and read them again later.

deliver_help.views: Views for each measured post, as displayed. Write 'not available' if they could not be read.
deliver_help.link_clicks: Link clicks for each measured post, as displayed. Write 'not available' if Threads does not show them, and do not calculate a click rate from a missing number.
deliver_help.where_read: Where the numbers came from and when. Example: 'Owner's screenshot of Threads insights, 2026-11-21 14:00 Taipei time'.
deliver_help.date_range: The start and end dates covered, with the time zone.

C-TH-POST.title: Publish one Threads post and confirm it
C-TH-POST.purpose: Publish the approved post once, under the right account, and hand back its public URL, because the post has to be live and exactly as approved before any click can be measured.

steps.do: Confirm the handle about to post is the agreed one, and look through its recent posts so you do not repeat the same content.
steps.evidence: The handle, and a note on the most recent posts you checked.

steps.do: Read the final text and any image for this post and check they fit the current Threads limits. Show the owner the exact text and get a clear yes before publishing.
steps.evidence: The final text, its character count, any image file, and the owner's approval message.

steps.do: If the message needs a follow-up post, plan it as a reply under the first post so everything stays in one thread. Do not publish it as several unrelated posts.
steps.evidence: A plan showing which post comes first and which one replies to it, or a note that one post is enough.

steps.do: Put the approved text, link, and image in the Threads post box, or hand them to the owner to paste, and check the preview matches the approved text. The agreed person presses Post once; if an upload is still in progress, let it finish and do not press Post again.
steps.evidence: Confirmation that the preview matched the approved text, who pressed Post, and when.

steps.do: After publishing, open the post's public URL and read back the full text, the author handle, and, for a follow-up, the post it sits under. If publishing seemed to fail, check the profile for the post before trying again so nothing is posted twice.
steps.evidence: The public URL, the text as it appears there, and the author handle.

blockers.do: If the owner has not said yes to this exact text, do not publish; show them the text and stop until they answer.
If the signed-in account is not the agreed handle, stop and ask the owner to switch accounts or to post it themselves.
If the agent's browser cannot post, give the owner the final text and link to paste, and ask them to send back the post URL.
If the post does not show up after publishing, check the profile again after a few minutes before any retry, and never post the same text twice.
If the link in the post does not open the product site, stop before publishing and fix the link with the owner.

deliver_help.post_url: The public link to the live post, opened and confirmed to load. Example: 'https://www.threads.net/@handle/post/...'.
deliver_help.published_text: The full text exactly as it appears on the live post, copied from the public page.
